notes: Current NCBI Bookshelf Hemolytic Transfusion Reaction was reread for delayed reaction timing and the anamnestic alloantibody mechanism.
NCBI Blood Groups and Red Cell Antigens — Kidd blood group was reread for the characteristic fall of Kidd antibody titers below detection and rapid rise after re-exposure.
Current NCBI Noninfectious Complications of Blood Transfusion was reread for prior sensitization, delayed antibody reappearance, and delayed red-cell destruction.
The official USMLE Content Outline 2026, Blood & Lymphoreticular System pp. 5–6, was visually verified and explicitly lists 'hemolysis, delayed' under reactions to blood components.

blueprint.competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

claim_audit.core_mechanism: Delayed hemolytic transfusion reactions can occur when a previously formed red-cell alloantibody has waned below pretransfusion detection and antigen re-exposure triggers a rapid secondary/anamnestic response.
claim_audit.kidd_specificity: Kidd antibodies are a classic cause of delayed hemolytic transfusion reactions because they may become undetectable between exposures and rise rapidly with re-exposure; anti-Jkᵃ therefore strengthens rather than overdetermines the vignette.
claim_audit.timing: A symptom-free interval followed by hemolysis about one week after transfusion is within the documented delayed-reaction window and clearly separates the case from an acute hemolytic transfusion reaction.
claim_audit.labs: Falling hemoglobin, increased indirect bilirubin and LDH, decreased haptoglobin, positive direct antiglobulin testing, and a newly detectable alloantibody are internally coherent with immune red-cell destruction.
claim_audit.distractor_1: Preexisting ABO antibodies produce an acute, often complement-mediated intravascular hemolytic reaction during or shortly after an incompatible transfusion, not the delayed anamnestic pattern shown.
claim_audit.distractor_2: TRALI is an acute pulmonary transfusion reaction involving donor anti-HLA/HNA antibodies and recipient neutrophil activation; the vignette has hemolysis without acute hypoxemic lung injury.
claim_audit.distractor_3: Anti-IgA-mediated anaphylaxis presents immediately with allergic/anaphylactic physiology, not delayed DAT-positive hemolysis.
claim_audit.distractor_4: Transfusion-associated graft-versus-host disease is caused by engrafted donor T cells and produces fever, rash, gastrointestinal disease, liver injury and marrow failure rather than a newly detectable red-cell alloantibody with isolated hemolysis.
claim_audit.blueprint_claim: The official 2026 USMLE Content Outline explicitly lists delayed hemolysis among reactions to blood components.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Remote prior transfusion establishes a plausible sensitizing exposure. A negative current antibody screen does not exclude a previously formed evanescent alloantibody. One week after re-exposure, biochemical hemolysis, a positive DAT, and newly detectable anti-Jkᵃ point to a secondary alloimmune response against transfused red cells.
adversarial_second_pass.delayed_serologic_reaction_challenge: This is not merely a delayed serologic transfusion reaction because there is objective hemolysis: hemoglobin falls, bilirubin and LDH rise, and haptoglobin falls.
adversarial_second_pass.acute_abo_challenge: The one-week interval and newly detectable minor-antigen alloantibody contradict an acute ABO-incompatible reaction.
adversarial_second_pass.trali_challenge: TRALI requires an acute lung-injury phenotype; none is present.
adversarial_second_pass.anti_iga_challenge: Anti-IgA anaphylaxis is immediate and allergic rather than hemolytic.
adversarial_second_pass.ta_gvhd_challenge: TA-GVHD can occur days to weeks after transfusion, so timing alone overlaps; however its characteristic donor-T-cell syndrome is absent and the DAT/anti-Jkᵃ hemolysis pattern directly supports DHTR.
adversarial_second_pass.complement_nuance: Kidd antibodies can bind complement and individual delayed reactions can include intravascular components. The keyed answer does not assert exclusively extravascular hemolysis, avoiding an overbroad mechanistic claim.
adversarial_second_pass.crossmatch_nuance: The case says crossmatch-compatible and pretransfusion screen negative, not that the patient had never formed an alloantibody; this is exactly the setting in which an evanescent antibody can be missed before an anamnestic response.
adversarial_second_pass.cueing_check: All five options are single mechanistic statements of comparable length and specificity. The correct option does not merely repeat the diagnosis or use a unique formatting cue.
adversarial_second_pass.unsupported_precision_check: The item uses a clinically supported one-week interval and does not depend on a narrow mandatory day, antibody titer, transfusion volume, or incidence estimate.
